context:
Treat the canonical schema-v2 bundle as input, not as the full hosted public
contract. Add hosted result identity, visibility, and trust semantics above
it without mutating the raw bundle format into a service-shaped payload.
description:
A hosted results platform is not just an upload endpoint. BenchBox needs a
durable contract for what a hosted result is, how it relates to the canonical
schema-v2 bundle, who can see it, how trustworthy it is, and which runs are
valid to compare or rank together.

This item defines the canonical hosted object model and the governance rules
around visibility, trust promotion, compatibility cohorts, privacy, and
public claims. Without this layer, the API, UI, and ranking surfaces will
drift into misleading or contradictory behavior.

**Phase assignment:** Phase 2-3 preparation. NOT required for Phase 1 (all
results are maintainer-curated, so trust labels and governance are trivial).
The cohort compatibility rules (w3) are partially relevant to Phase 1 compare
views but can be handled with simple same-benchmark/same-scale validation
without a full governance model.

anti_patterns.dont: allow ranking before compatibility cohorts are defined
treat every public upload as equally trustworthy
anti_patterns.instead: make trust labels explicit in the contract
anti_patterns.why: self-reported and curated results carry different weight

preserves.behavior: BenchBox does not imply TPC certification or equivalent official standing for ordinary hosted submissions
Canonical BenchBox result bundles remain downloadable and distinguishable from any derived hosted metadata

work_units.notes:
Separate three distinct identifiers: (1) bundle hash - content-addressable,
immutable; (2) submission ID - generated on ingest, survives re-upload;
(3) public result ID - stable permalink, may be minted after curation.
Define allowed ingest status transitions: pending → validated → published,
plus rejected and withdrawn. Output: identity-model.md draft.
work_units.summary: Define hosted result identity, immutable bundle contract, and ingest status model

work_units.notes:
Cover private, unlisted, public self-reported, public curated, and public
verified states or an explicitly revised equivalent.
work_units.summary: Define visibility states and trust labels for hosted results

work_units.notes: Prevent incompatible runs from being mixed into misleading comparisons.
work_units.summary: Define cohort and ranking eligibility rules for comparison and leaderboards

work_units.notes: Decide what system metadata may be public, redactable, or removable after submission.
work_units.summary: Define privacy, redaction, retention, and data-removal policy

work_units.notes:
Produce a single hosted-results-contract.md that specifies:
- What fields the submission endpoint accepts and returns
- Which visibility states and trust labels the explorer must render
- Which cohort fields must match for a compare view to be valid
- What privacy/redaction/removal operations are supported
This doc is the authoritative input for design-results-ingest (Phase 3
API design) and the explorer frontend trust-label implementation.
work_units.summary: Document the contract for CLI, API, and frontend consumers
